text:
sven: FYI seeing a big eviction wave in asia-southeast1 around 03:10 UTC, lots of gpu nodes gone in ~2m. Pods keep bouncing.
maia: ugh. any obvious error in the node events?
aj: paste from kube events earlier:
```
Warning  Eviction  2m (x45 over 2m)  kubelet, gke-asia-pool  node(s) had Kubelet eviction: "ran out of resource: ephemeral-storage"
Normal   NodeTerminated 1m            GCE  Instance preempted (SUSPENDED)
```
natalie: that looks like preemptible kills + disk pressure. Are these our spot gpu pools or something else?
sven: yes these are the `gpu-ephemeral-asia` nodepool (preemptible). CA tried to scale but hit `maxNodes` on pool and we have no on-demand fallback.
cluster-autoscaler-bot: [03:12] ScaleDownCandidate: pods failed to find nodes -> failed scaling due to quota/limits on pool `gpu-ephemeral-asia`
aj: we saw similar in eu but there we have `gpu-standby-on-demand` pool and CA can spin those up. asia doesn't have that (region soft-limit + quota work pending).
maia: two quick mitigations: 1) add a tiny always-on on-demand pool (1-2 nodes) with tolerations for gpu jobs; 2) increase pool maxNodes for spot pool temporarily.
sven: options and tradeoffs?
aj: cost math: if we add 2 on-demand n1-gpu nodes, cost bump ~+8% for GPUs during incident windows but latency/failed-job cost >> that.
natalie: can we instead set CA to fall back to smaller cpu-only nodes and run evicted work on cpu where possible (best-effort)? Some jobs require GPUs though.
ops-oncall: some jobs are GPU-only (training infra), but inference batch jobs can degrade to CPU mode. We should tag workloads with PriorityClass and tolerations.
maia: plan I propose:
- create nodepool `gpu-fallback-od-asia` (1 min, 2 max), taint `gpu-fallback=true:NoSchedule`, nodeSelector for `gpu-workloads:allowed`
- patch kube-CA expander to prefer on-demand pool when `gpu-ephemeral-asia` is below 10% capacity
- add short-lived quota bump request to GCP for asia GPUs (ticket)
- instrument `eviction` alert to hit #eng-infra with aggregated counts

aj: example nodepool YAML (gcloud style) to create quickly:
```
# create fallback pool (pseudo)
gcloud container node-pools create gpu-fallback-od-asia \
  --cluster=prod-asia --machine-type=n1-standard-16 --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-t4,count=1 \
  --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=0 --max-nodes=2 \
  --node-taints=gpu-fallback=true:NoSchedule --labels=gpu-workloads=allowed
```
maia: and a small Pod toleration example for batch inference:
```
tolerations:
- key: "gpu-fallback"
  operator: "Equal"
  value: "true"
  effect: "NoSchedule"
```
sven: nice. who can create the pool & change CA policy now?
aj: I can do the gcloud create, but need IAM for nodepool create. If ops-oncall can open the quota ticket and approve, I can run it.
ops-oncall: opening a GCP quota ticket now, will paste the request ID.
cluster-autoscaler-bot: [03:25] CA: Pod pending - triggering scale up candidates: gpu-fallback-od-asia (preferred)
natalie: quick thought — make sure we set nodeAffinity with `topology.gke.io/zone` to keep fallback nodes spread across zones; otherwise a zonal preemption hits all.
maia: good call. also enable `preemptibleReplacementPolicy`? (if cloud supports it) so CA prefers replacement in different zone.
sven: action items:
- aj: create the `gpu-fallback-od-asia` pool (IAM + gcloud) — target: 03:40 UTC
- ops-oncall: quota ticket ID + approval — 03:30 UTC
- maia: patch CA expander + add alert rules — 04:00 UTC
- natalie: add toleration docs and quickstart snippet for teams — 05:00 UTC

aj: starting the create now, will post logs and node names when ready.
ops-oncall: quota ticket created: Q-24512. mentioning infra-quota@ and eng-manage. :thumbsup:
aj: pool created, nodes `gpu-fallback-od-asia-1a`, `-1b` are registering. CA picked them up and scheduled 3 pending pods.
maia: :tada: monitoring latency and failed-pod rate. dropping from 22->2 errors/min so far.
sven: great. follow-up: we should document a DR playbook for region spot purge and run a cost simulation for permanently keeping 1 fallback node vs. on-demand auto-launch frequency.
natalie: I'll draft a short doc and run cost sims for 1x t4 vs. on-demand bursts.
aj: logs and final diff:
```
kubectl get nodes --label-columns=gpu-workloads
NAME                             STATUS   ROLES    AGE
gpu-fallback-od-asia-1a          Ready    <none>   2m
gpu-fallback-od-asia-1b          Ready    <none>   1m
```
sven: awesome. closing here but please ping #eng-infra if anything re-evicts. thanks all. :heart:
